title: Adopt lib/errors.js in the three largest route files (proxy, workspace-api, dispatch)
description:
From the 2026-06-11 Drift & Coherence Review (LIN-419, Finding 1, medium).

`lib/errors.js` is the canonical error-envelope module (LIN-36) but only `routes/workspace.js` and now `routes/proxy.js` (LIN-417) import it; every other route hand-rolls inline `res.status(4xx).json({ error })` — 246 inline 4xx sites across routes/, concentrated in proxy.js (106), workspace-api.js (80), dispatch.js (42).

Scope: in those three files only, replace inline `res.status(4xx).json({ error })` with `jsonError`/`badRequest`/`notFound`/`unauthorized` from lib/errors.js. The shapes are already wire-compatible (`{ error, ...extra }`), so assert no behavior change with existing tests. NOT a fleet-wide sweep — touch only these three files. Leaves the LIN-417 structured envelope as the model for richer cases.

comments.body:
Adopted `lib/errors.js` helpers across the three largest route files.

**PR:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/505
**Commit:** 7f790dc
**CI:** green (unit + all 4 E2E shards + ci-success all pass)

**What changed:** Replaced inline `res.status(...).json({ error })` in `routes/proxy.js`, `routes/workspace-api.js`, `routes/dispatch.js` with `badRequest`/`notFound`/`unauthorized` (plain 4xx bodies) and `jsonError` (status+extra-field bodies, plus 5xx/403/413/429 with no named helper). Net 335 insertions / 379 deletions.

**Wire-compatible:** every response keeps its exact `{ error, ...extra }` shape and status code. Multi-field bodies (`detail`, `code`, `matchCount`, `freeTier`, `message`) preserved via `jsonError`'s extra arg. Verified zero remaining inline `res.status(4xx).json({error})` sites in the three files.

**Scope held:** only the three named files. The LIN-417 structured envelope (`workspaceUnavailableEnvelope`) left in place as the richer model. The `trashed-signal` unit test's source-shape assertion was widened to accept the `jsonError(res, 409, …)` form. Full unit suite: 1815 pass / 0 fail.

Ready for review.
